headline: KENORLAND AND TARGA LAUNCH $3.9M PHASE 2 DRILL AT OPINACA GOLD DISCOVERY — 700m STEP-OUT FOLLOWS 13.88 g/t AU INTERCEPT IN JAMES BAY, QUEBEC
snippet: Kenorland Minerals (TSXV: KLD) and Targa Exploration Corp. (CSE: TEX) announced Phase 2 drilling has commenced at the Opinaca Project in the James Bay Region of Quebec — a $3.9 million program comprising up to 4,400 metres of diamond drilling that opens with a 700-metre westward step-out from where Phase 1 hole 25OPDD007 returned 13.88 g/t gold over 3.65 metres, including 166.14 g/t Au over 0.30 metres with visible gold. Phase 1 intersected gold in 7 of 8 holes across a 4-kilometre target area with no prior drilling, establishing one of Quebec's most compelling new grassroots discoveries; Phase 2 also evaluates regional targets identified through systematic mapping.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER HITS WOODJAM'S LONGEST HIGH-GRADE INTERCEPT — 48.5m AT 3.32% CU WITHIN 266m AT 0.97% AT DEERHORN, BC SHARES JUMP 14%
snippet: Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSXV: VCU) reported that drill hole DH26-136 at its Deerhorn deposit within the Woodjam Project in central British Columbia intersected 266.0 metres grading 0.97% copper (plus 0.06 g/t Au and 4.29 g/t Ag), including 107.7 metres at 2.01% Cu and a 48.5-metre high-grade core at 3.32% Cu, 0.23 g/t Au, and 16.59 g/t Ag — the longest high-grade intersection in the project's history from the recently completed 6,055-metre summer program. The result comes as COMEX copper holds near $6.57 per pound following a fresh record earlier this week, and Vizsla shares gained 14% on the announcement.

headline: COPPER LME WAREHOUSE RUN HITS 42ND STRAIGHT DAY — CASH SPREAD REACHES $434/TONNE 5-YEAR HIGH AS HALF OF REMAINING STOCKS EARMARKED FOR WITHDRAWAL
snippet: LME copper warehouse inventories fell for a 42nd consecutive session to 204,975 tonnes — their lowest level since 2014's extended drawdown — and nearly half of remaining stocks are already earmarked for cancellation and withdrawal, stoking fears of a physical shortage that could dwarf the August 12 Comex record of $6.7270 per pound. The cash-to-three-month backwardation briefly hit $434 per tonne, a five-year extreme, as buyers compete for immediately available metal; Goldman Sachs simultaneously issued a note questioning whether the rally has run its course, setting up a contested narrative heading into September.

headline: ONTARIO LOCKS IN $17.5M FOR ELECTRA'S COBALT SULPHATE REFINERY — NORTH AMERICA'S FIRST BATTERY-GRADE COBALT PROCESSOR ON TRACK FOR Q4 2026 COMMISSIONING
snippet: Electra Battery Materials Corporation finalized definitive agreements on August 26 with Invest Ontario for C$17.5 million in funding toward construction of its cobalt sulphate refinery in Temiskaming Shores, Ontario — the last major financing piece in an ~$84 million capital stack that includes a $20 million U.S. Department of Defense grant and $20 million from the federal government. The refinery, targeting commissioned operations in Q4 2026 and commercial production in Q4 2027, would be North America's first battery-grade cobalt sulphate facility, directly addressing the Western supply chain's most acute processing gap for EV battery cathode materials.

headline: U.S. GOLDMINING PASSES 5,000 METRES AT WHISTLER GOLD-COPPER IN ALASKA — CONGRESS TOURS PROJECT AS CRITICAL MINERALS POLICY TAILWINDS BUILD
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (Nasdaq: USGO) disclosed that 11 diamond core drill holes totalling over 5,000 metres have been completed across eight distinct targets in the Whistler Orbit, with initial assays expected in coming weeks and drilling advancing on schedule and on budget toward a 6,000-metre minimum program. On August 24, the Company hosted members of the U.S. House of Representatives on a Western Caucus Foundation field tour, providing a platform to showcase Whistler's strategic value to domestic gold-copper supply chains and critical mineral security — reinforcing the project's policy positioning at a time when federal permitting support for Alaskan resource projects is accelerating.

headline: ONE BULLION STARTS FIRST DRILL AT VUMBA GOLD PROJECT, BOTSWANA — 10-HOLE HQ PROGRAM TARGETS STRUCTURAL CORRIDORS NEAR 679 g/t SURFACE GOLD
snippet: One Bullion Ltd. (TSXV: OBUL) announced that diamond drilling has commenced at its Vumba Gold Project in Botswana, opening a 3,000-metre HQ program across 10 holes targeting three priority structural corridors identified through an integrated review of historical drilling, surface geochemistry, and the Company's recently completed high-resolution airborne magnetic survey. The program is designed to test the orientation, continuity, and plunge of known mineralized structures, building on prior artisanal sampling that returned a headline 679 g/t gold grab sample — one of the more eye-catching surface results from an emerging Botswana explorer.

headline: GOLD EDGES TO $4,650 AS MARKETS HOLD BREATH FOR WARSH'S INAUGURAL JACKSON HOLE KEYNOTE FRIDAY
snippet: Spot gold drifted 0.2% higher to $4,648.90 on Thursday, August 27, recovering from Wednesday's 1.4% one-day decline triggered by a hotter-than-expected July PCE print, as investors position ahead of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's inaugural speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday — the most consequential policy communication of his tenure so far. Markets are pricing a 60% probability of no September rate change; gold's ability to recover despite short-term yield pressure is being read by strategists as evidence of structural demand that rate-path noise cannot dislodge, with Goldman Sachs ($4,900), JPMorgan ($4,500 Q4), and Bank of America ($4,360) all carrying forward targets above current spot.

headline: K2 GOLD MAPS HIGH-GRADE AG-AU-CU POLYMETALLIC SYSTEM AT MORNINGSTAR — 613-SAMPLE PROGRAM OUTLINES MULTIPLE TRENDS IN CALIFORNIA
snippet: K2 Gold Corporation (TSXV: KTO) announced results from 613 rock samples collected at its Morningstar Target in Inyo County, California as part of its 2026 surface program: the dataset identified discrete, spatially coherent trends of high-grade silver, gold, and copper values from grab and chip samples, outlining a polymetallic system with multiple high-grade shoots. The work sets up a drill-ready target in a well-established mining district, expanding K2's portfolio of drill candidates as silver's 19% August surge has renewed retail and institutional interest in silver-leveraged exploration stories.

headline: VR RESOURCES INTERSECTS 2,892 FEET OF NEAR-CONTINUOUS MOLY-COPPER-TUNGSTEN-SILVER-ZINC AT NEW BOSTON, NEVADA — SHARES POST TRIPLE-DIGIT GAINS
snippet: VR Resources Limited (TSXV: VRR) reported that drill hole NB26-003 at the New Boston Project in Nevada delivered near-continuous molybdenum-copper-tungsten-silver-zinc mineralization across 2,892 feet of core — a result that triggered triple-digit share gains and positions New Boston as one of the more unusual and potentially significant polymetallic porphyry-style targets to emerge in the Western U.S. this summer. The multi-metal character of the system, if grades prove economic on assay, could attract attention from a broad range of strategic acquirers given critical minerals policy momentum around domestic tungsten and molybdenum supply.

headline: WHY SILVER IS OUTPERFORMING GOLD IN 2026 — A SIX-YEAR SUPPLY DEFICIT MEETS EXPLOSIVE INDUSTRIAL DEMAND
snippet: GoldSilver's analysis argues that silver's August outperformance — up 19% versus gold's 15% — is not a short-term momentum trade but the structural consequence of six consecutive years of physical supply deficits now colliding with accelerating industrial consumption from AI data centers, solar photovoltaics, and EV systems. The piece points out that speculative positioning remains near the 20th percentile of the past 60 weeks, meaning institutional money has not yet piled into silver, which historically precedes the most violent legs of silver bull markets when the industrial and investment demand cycles synchronize.
